title: V
author: StańczykOne
desc:
This schedule was designed by proportionally adjusting the weekly training volume, intensity, and frequency for large and small muscle groups—determined based on the approximate volumetric sizes of the body’s muscle groups—and by taking recovery capacity into account. 
So, the goal was to create the most optimal muscle-building schedule for individuals who are committed to making exercise a part of their lives but do not earn a financial income from it or pursue it as a profession.
To be able to perform this schedule effectively, it is essential that you have trained for at least a few years, have firmly established the mind-muscle connection, have mastered the exercises, and have a clear understanding of the concept of failure so that you can exert sufficient effort.
Before you start the schedule in earnest, please try it out for a week or two first and listen to your body. 
To prevent the fatigue caused by the schedule and which will build up over time, a one-week deload/autoregulation week has been added at the end of each month, i.e. at the end of each four-week period. During this week, you may feel as though you are following a powerlifting schedule. Furthermore, if you feel sufficiently refreshed and able to continue, you can skip this week entirely; however, as a recommendation, do not skip it. You can view this week as an opportunity to break your personal records and rest both mentally and physically. However, if you feel exhausted before the four-week period ends and feel you can no longer continue training, you can repeat the same deload/autoregulation week after two weeks and resume the schedule where you left off.

We also recommend combining this schedule with a cardio routine. In five-day weeks, on Tuesdays and Saturdays, and in four-day weeks, on Wednesdays and Saturdays, it would be beneficial to incorporate 40-minute LISS-style cardio sessions; during deload/autoregulation weeks, you may consider also include 20-minutes HIIT-style cardio sessions for each one of three days.

P.S 1: This workout basically consists of high-effort work sets. Therefore, you must know how to make a work set to achieve gains and benefits. If you have no idea what a work set is or what high intensity mean, please do not follow this program.
P.S 2: You should do warm-up sets before your work sets and warm up your body thoroughly. Furthermore, mobility exercises are extremely important and should always be included in your schedule. Do not overlook this.

Some tips:
1) You should time your rest periods between sets carefully and avoid moving on to the next set before you’re ready.
2) If you feel not truly good or your muscles say “enough,” you should stop and skip the next set. Even move directly to the next exercise.
3) Some exercises require assistance. If you are working out alone, you need to ask someone for help and support. Rest assured, they will be happy to do so.
4)In some cases, you may consider the using straps, wraps, or a weight belt etc.
